title: Ladakh packing guide for women
description: What to wear in Ladakh: layers, footwear and modesty notes for women. Packing lists by trip length, altitude tips and looks at three budgets.
intro: Ladakh is cold, dry and bright. The air is thin, the sun is fierce and the nights drop below freezing. You do not need glamour here. You need layers, good shoes and sun protection. Here are looks, a modesty note for villages and monasteries, and packing lists for five, seven and ten days.

sections.heading: Modesty note
sections.body: Ladakh is a Buddhist and Muslim region, and people dress conservatively in villages and monasteries. Cover your shoulders and knees when you enter a monastery. Remove shoes and hats. Avoid very short shorts or tight outfits in towns such as Leh. Thermal layers with trousers and long jackets cover everything and keep you warm. Most visitors wear trekking clothes, so you will not stand out.
tips: Cover shoulders and knees in monasteries.
Remove hats and shoes before entering a prayer hall.
Avoid outfits that expose the midriff in villages.
A scarf covers your head and neck from sun and dust.

sections.heading: Layering system
sections.body: Layers beat one big jacket. Start with a thermal base layer. Add a fleece or wool mid layer. Finish with a wind-proof, insulated jacket. In the sun, you may take off two layers. At night, you will put them all on. Cotton holds moisture and makes you cold. Pick merino, polyester blends or fleece.
tips: Outer: down jacket or insulated shell.
Extras: gloves, beanie, neck gaiter, thick socks.

sections.heading: Outfit formulas
sections.body: Each with footwear and one accessory.

looks.name: Town day, Leh
pieces: Thermal top and leggings, about ₹900 (Decathlon, Uniqlo Heattech)
Fleece jacket, about ₹1,200 (Decathlon or Vero Moda knit)
Footwear: sturdy sneakers with thick socks, about ₹1,800

looks.name: Monastery and lake day
pieces: Wool-blend sweater, about ₹2,500 (Uniqlo or Marks & Spencer)
Water-resistant trekking trousers, about ₹2,500 (Decathlon or Wildcraft)
looks.why: Trousers and a sweater cover you at monasteries and keep you warm at lakes.

looks.name: Evening stay
pieces: Fleece-lined joggers and a hoodie, about ₹2,000 (H&M or Uniqlo)
looks.why: Camps and homestays are cold at night.

looks.name: Trek or Pangong overnight
pieces: Down jacket, about ₹7,000 (Wildcraft, Decathlon or Columbia)
looks.why: Pangong is minus degrees at night. A real down jacket is worth it.

sections.heading: Packing list by trip length
sections.body: Five days: two thermal sets, two fleece or sweaters, one down jacket, two pairs of trekking trousers, five pairs of socks, one pair of boots, sunglasses, sunscreen and lip balm. Seven days: add another thermal set, an extra sweater and gloves. Ten days: add a spare pair of trousers, a rain shell and a second hat. Laundry is slow in the cold, so pack extras.
tips: Ten days: a large duffel plus a daypack.
Pack medicine for altitude. Ask your doctor before you go.

sections.heading: On the plane
sections.body: Wear your bulkiest layers. Put on trousers, a thermal, a fleece and your boots. Put the down jacket in the cabin bag or wear it. You land at 3,500 metres. It is cold and bright, so keep sunglasses handy.

sections.heading: Climate note
sections.body: May to September is the main season. Days are 15 to 25 degrees and nights are 0 to 8. In October, nights fall below zero. Winter is minus 15 or lower, and most tourist camps close. Sun is strong at altitude, so wear sunscreen and sunglasses year round.

sections.heading: Colour and silhouette
sections.body: Ladakh is stark and bright, so colour pops against rock and sky. Mustard, red, teal and magenta look striking in photos. Layered silhouettes are practical. Choose a fitted base and looser outer layers. A long jacket keeps your back warm. Pick colours near your face that suit you, such as a neck gaiter or beanie.
tips: Bright jackets look great in photos.
Keep base layers in neutral colours so they mix.
Pick a colour for your beanie that suits your skin.
Buy locally woven shawls in Leh.

sections.heading: What to stop buying for Ladakh
sections.body: Stop buying cotton thermals. Stop buying fashion sneakers with no grip. Stop buying one thick jacket instead of layers. Stop buying jeans, which stay cold and heavy. Skip makeup. Pack a heavy moisturiser and lip balm.

faq.q: What should women wear in Ladakh?
faq.a: Wear thermal layers, fleece, a down jacket, trekking trousers and sturdy shoes. Cover shoulders and knees in monasteries.

faq.q: Can I wear jeans in Ladakh?
faq.a: You can, but jeans are cold and slow to dry. Trekking trousers or fleece-lined pants are better.

faq.q: How many layers do I need?
faq.a: Three: a thermal base, a mid layer and a wind-proof outer. Add gloves and a hat.
Yes. UV at altitude is strong. Wear sunglasses with UV protection, plus sunscreen.

cta.headline: Which jacket colour is actually yours?
cta.sub: One selfie, five questions: your season, your palette, your three strengths. Pick the layers that suit you. Free.
